verdict.rationale: Lithic's ASA (Authorization Stream Access) is well documented as an HTTP endpoint that receives POST requests during live authorization and must respond with an approval/decline decision, and Auth Rules/shadow mode let developers control decision logic and level (program/account/card) [lithic-docs-2, lithic-docs-16, lithic-docs-17, lithic-docs-24]. However the evidence pack never documents the network's specific time budget or a configurable timeout/fallback behavior developers control if their endpoint doesn't respond in time. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the ASA response time window and a configurable fallback decision (approve/decline-by-default) mechanism.
